doc.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

title: Portrait of Dr. Moon: short, muscular acrobat who got free haircuts
summary: Dr. Moon was about 35, under five feet, an acrobat with rigging on the platform, and a rich man who took free barber college haircuts.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So, uh, getting back to what we did when we get to the town. Uh-huh. After, after we set up the platform and got that straightened out, we would get on the back of this bus.

Uh-huh. Doc, this Doc Moon was a kind of versatile guy. How old was he at that time? Who, Doc Moon? Yeah. Oh, he wasn't old at that time. Uh, Doc was about, uh, oh, I imagine about 35 years old. What did he look like?

He was a little bit of short guy. He was almost a midget. He was a little less than five feet tall. Thin? No. Very muscular. Very muscular. Very muscular. In fact, uh, he, he, uh, the part of the show, he used to do, uh, tricks. He had a rigging that they set up too on the platform. Tricks on the barbell, you know. He was an acrobat, huh?
That's right. That's the, that's the thing I wanted to get out. He was an acrobat. And a darn good one. Oh, yeah? Yeah.

The funny thing about Doc Moon, the guy had a lot of money. He did? But, uh, he never paid for a haircut. Uh, during those days of Mola Barber College used to give free haircuts. Ha! Ha! Ha! Doc would wait, wait until we got to a big town like St. Louis around Chicago. We played, we never played directly in the big towns. We played outskirts like Gary, Indiana. Yes. Doc would wait until he got there, and I'm going to go over the Barber College and go get a haircut. Ha! And some of them haircuts was really something to see, man. Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! That always stuck to me as a funny thing, this cat with all that money. Ha! Ha! Ha! Looked like somebody had cut it with a knife. Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha!
